hints: Notice the question starts from the weight of the rocket, which means the gravitational pull of the Earth on the rocket.
Recall a Newton third law pair must be the same type of force with the two bodies swapped, so look for a gravitational force on the other body.
Compare the exhaust-gas forces and air resistance with a rocket-on-Earth gravitational pull to see which swaps Earth and rocket.
walkthrough: Identify what weight is: it is the gravitational force exerted by the Earth on the rocket, acting downward toward the Earth.
State the Newton third law rule: the pair must be the same kind of interaction, equal in size and opposite in direction, with the agent and object interchanged.
Apply the swap: if one force is Earth on rocket and gravitational, the other must be rocket on Earth and gravitational.
Check the distractors: air resistance involves air, and the two exhaust-gas forces form a separate contact-thrust pair between rocket and gases.
Therefore the only force that is gravitational and exerted by the rocket on the Earth matches the rule. This is option D.

options.A: Air resistance is a contact drag force on the rocket from the air, not a gravitational force involving the Earth.
options.B: This is the thrust force from the exhaust on the rocket, which pairs with the rocket pushing on the exhaust, not with the weight.
options.C: This is one half of the rocket-exhaust thrust pair, whereas weight belongs to a gravitational interaction with the Earth.
options.D: Weight is the gravitational force of the Earth on the rocket, so its pair is the equal gravitational force of the rocket on the Earth.
